source.title: Understanding Generalization in Adversarial Training via the Bias-Variance Decomposition
source.authors: Yaodong Yu; Zi-Tong Yang; Edgar Dobriban; Jacob Steinhardt; Yi Ma

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own results on the generalization gap in adversarially trained models, extending the study of generalization to a different training setting. It does not test the listed versions' standard-training conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures bias, variance, risk, and training/test errors under adversarial training and related settings. Results from cited prior work are not extracted as rows. Figure-only sweeps are represented by the paper's accompanying qualitative descriptions, without estimating plotted values.
record.test_reason: The width sweep in Figures 7 and 14 measures training and held-out classification error as networks widen, bearing on V2 in a new setting: adversarially trained WideResNets with weight decay. The other experiments measure different aspects of generalization and do not test the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the conclusion for the principal image settings. The authors find increasing bias that dominates risk and unimodal variance peaking near robust interpolation, use these patterns to evaluate conceptual explanations, and identify unlabeled data and adversarial pre-training as promising ways to reduce bias. These patterns have explicit exceptions, including low-dimensional box models, fixed-noise training, and shifted evaluation distributions.
record.recipe_differences: Studies adversarial training and related robustness procedures, using bias-variance decompositions; the listed versions primarily concern standard training, optimizers, architecture, regularization, sharpness, and memorization.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured bias-variance patterns vary with training method (randomized smoothing versus fixed Gaussian-perturbed data), dimension (2D versus higher-dimensional box data), early stopping, width, evaluation distribution, and augmentation severity.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the principal image experiments, bias grows with adversarial radius and dominates risk, while variance peaks near robust interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial radius produces characteristic bias-variance curves in image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Early stopping lowers variance and slightly raises bias, shifting the variance peak toward smaller perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early stopping changes adversarial training's bias-variance balance.

fits_no_version.finding: Dynamic Gaussian noise reproduces the main adversarial-training pattern; fixed Gaussian perturbations produce increasing variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic and fixed training noise produce different bias-variance behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Low-dimensional box models lack the unimodal variance pattern; higher-dimensional box models and the tested logistic models reproduce it, with approximate bias monotonicity for logistic regression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dimensionality and data distribution affect adversarial bias-variance behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Bias improves only marginally at larger widths; unlabeled data and adversarial pre-training reduce bias, and unlabeled data also reduces variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width, additional data, and pre-training affect adversarial bias and variance differently.

fits_no_version.finding: Evaluation distribution changes the perturbation-radius curves, while increasing AugMix severity lowers bias, variance, and risk.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distribution shift and augmentation strength alter bias-variance behavior.

record.problems: Most curve results are presented in figures and described qualitatively without numerical values or reported uncertainty. Bias-variance estimates use partitioned training data, changing the training sample size from n to n/2. The claim versions' standard-training conditions are not directly evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted; 17 rows retained, below the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: No comparison of fixed random-label fitting, random-label held-out accuracy, and natural-label generalization.

The original one-hidden-layer ReLU, MNIST/downsampled-CIFAR-10, no-explicit-regularization, convergence-trained setting is untested. The robust 2% interpolation criterion is not the claim's zero training error.
No matched convolutional versus fully connected comparison, learned local connectivity experiment, or convolutional-to-fully-connected initialization.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or tuning-budget comparison.
No batch-size sweep or large-batch recipe comparison.
No dropout experiment or joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
No magnitude-aware weight sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: R11 needs the actual standard training-error and standard test-error trends across width, especially after training error reaches zero. Also distinguish that point from the robust 2% threshold at width 4. The supplied figure text contains axes and legends but no readable curve coordinates; the prose describes bias and variance only, so a directional V2 verdict cannot be established.
missing.locator: Section 5, Figure 7 right panel; Appendix C.2, Figure 14 right panel

record.verdict_notes: Different training conditions alone do not exclude the width sweep from bearing on V2 as a new-setting test. However, smaller bias is not equivalent to lower classification error, and marginal improvement is not evidence of an absent effect. No V2 label is justified by the readable results supplied here. States for rows linked to none describe their inability to establish a listed version, not whether their separate reported findings occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with generalization on natural labels under standard training.
The width sweep uses adversarial training, not the specified standard-training setting; it does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected models under the specified standard-training conditions.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on the specified image-classification or language benchmarks.
Does not vary batch size or test large-batch training.
Measures bias and variance, not magnitude-aware sharpness or the ranking of sharpness against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: Wide-ResNet-28-10
rows.operation_detail: L-infinity adversarial training with increasing perturbation size; measures bias, variance, risk, and training/test errors.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, risk, and standard/robust training and standard test error as functions of ε.
rows.baseline: ε = 0 reference is shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Bias increases monotonically; variance increases then decreases, with its peak near the robust interpolation threshold; bias is the dominant term in risk.
rows.note: Qualitative result stated in the text; plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Perturbation-radius effects on bias and variance do not measure any listed version. The radius is ε/255, with ε from 0 to 20, rather than an unnormalized radius from 0 to 20.

rows.subject: PreActResNet18
rows.operation_detail: L-infinity adversarial training with increasing perturbation size; measures bias and variance behavior.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of ε.
rows.baseline: ε = 0 reference is shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Bias increases monotonically; variance is unimodal and peaks near the robust interpolation threshold; bias dominates risk.
rows.note: The paper states that properties P1–P4 hold; no plotted values are reconstructed.
rows.check: No listed version concerns this bias-variance sweep. The perturbation radius is ε/255.

rows.subject: Wide-ResNet-28-10
rows.operation_detail: L-infinity adversarial training stopped at epoch 100; measures bias and variance behavior.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, risk, and robust interpolation threshold as functions of ε.
rows.baseline: Fully trained model in Figure 1; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: The variance peak occurs earlier but still coincides with the robust interpolation threshold; the four stated properties continue to hold. At small ε, risk is lower due to decreased variance while bias increases slightly.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes the earlier peak and the small-ε bias/variance tradeoff.
rows.check: Early-stopping effects on bias and variance do not measure a listed version; partial is not a claim-relative state here.

rows.subject: Wide-ResNet-28-10

rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of noise variance.
rows.baseline: Noise variance 0 reference is shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Properties P1–P4 continue to hold, as for adversarial training.
rows.note: The paper describes the qualitative curves but does not give their plotted values.
rows.check: Randomized-smoothing bias and variance do not measure a listed version.

rows.subject: Wide-ResNet-28-10
rows.operation_detail: Training on Gaussian-perturbed data with increasing noise variance; measures bias and variance behavior.

conditions.value: Training images perturbed once at the beginning of training

rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of noise variance.
rows.baseline: Noise variance 0 reference is shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Bias and variance both increase monotonically; properties P2 and P3 do not hold.
rows.note: The paper distinguishes this fixed-noise training from randomized smoothing.
rows.check: Increasing variance under fixed input noise is not a reversal of any listed version.

rows.subject: Fully connected network (three hidden layers with 100 nodes each)
rows.size_stated: three hidden layers with 100 nodes each
rows.operation_detail: L-infinity adversarial training on the 2D box example with increasing perturbation size; measures bias and variance.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of ε.
rows.baseline: ε = 0 reference is shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Bias increases monotonically; variance increases monotonically rather than being unimodal.
rows.note: The text says P1 and P4 hold, while P2 and P3 do not; its sentence appears to repeat P4 when describing the variance.
rows.check: The dimensionality-dependent bias-variance finding does not measure a listed version. Table 1 confirms that P2 and P3 fail; the reference to P4 failing in Section 4.1 is a textual error.

rows.subject: Adversarial logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Adversarial logistic regression on mixture-of-Gaussians data with increasing perturbation size; measures bias and variance.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of ε.
rows.baseline: ε = 0 reference is shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Variance increases then decreases and peaks at the robust interpolation threshold; bias dominates variance. Bias initially decreases before eventually increasing.
rows.note: The paper says P2–P4 hold, while P1 does not quite hold.
rows.check: Logistic-regression bias and variance under changing perturbation radius do not measure a listed version. The initial bias decrease is across perturbation radii, not training time.

rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of ε.
rows.baseline: ε = 0 reference is shown; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Variance increases then decreases and peaks at the robust interpolation threshold; bias dominates variance. Bias initially decreases before eventually increasing.

rows.subject: WideResNet-28-[width]
rows.operation_detail: Increases width factor during L-infinity adversarial training and measures bias, variance, risk, and training/test errors.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, risk, and robust/standard training and standard test error as functions of width.
rows.baseline: Other width factors in the sweep; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Making models wider only marginally improves bias beyond a certain width factor. In Appendix C.2, bias is described as monotonically decreasing; variance increases before the robust interpolation threshold and changes little after it.
rows.note: The figures show the sweep, but the text provides only qualitative descriptions.
rows.check: The width sweep includes the relevant training/test-error measures, but its extracted value reports bias and variance instead. Marginal bias improvement cannot establish whether test error keeps falling after zero training error. Appendix C.2 places the robust interpolation threshold at width 4, using a 2% robust-error criterion rather than literal zero error. Training also includes weight decay and a fixed 200-epoch schedule.

rows.subject: Wide-ResNet-28-10
rows.operation_detail: Adds unlabeled data to L-infinity adversarial training; measures standard and adversarial bias and variance.
rows.measure: Standard and adversarial bias and variance.
rows.baseline: Standard adversarial training; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Additional unlabeled data significantly decreases both standard bias and variance; it improves both adversarial bias and adversarial variance.
rows.note: The paper reports qualitative changes; plotted values are not reconstructed.
rows.check: Adding unlabeled data does not test any listed version.

rows.subject: Wide-ResNet-28-10
rows.operation_detail: Uses an adversarially pre-trained model for initialization before adversarial training; measures standard and adversarial bias and variance.
rows.measure: Standard and adversarial bias and variance.
rows.baseline: Standard adversarial training; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Pre-training mainly decreases standard bias and mainly improves adversarial bias.
rows.note: The text says pre-training mainly affects bias; it does not state that variance decreases.
rows.check: Adversarial pre-training does not test V3's convolutional-to-fully-connected initialization comparison or another listed version.

rows.subject: Wide-ResNet-28-10
rows.operation_detail: Combines additional unlabeled data and adversarial pre-training; measures bias and clean error.
rows.baseline: Standard adversarial training; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Using both further decreases bias, leading to a smaller clean error.
rows.note: The paper reports the direction of change but gives no numerical values in the text.
rows.check: Combining unlabeled data and adversarial pre-training does not test a listed version.

rows.subject: L-infinity adversarially trained models
rows.operation_detail: Evaluates bias, variance, and risk on CIFAR10-C across corruption severity levels.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of ε and corruption severity.
rows.baseline: Severity 0 corresponds to the standard CIFAR10 test set; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: On CIFAR10-C, bias becomes U-shaped and variance changes to a double-descent-shaped curve with two dips. At small ε, both bias and variance are smaller than for standard training.
rows.note: OOD evaluation is outside the ordinary held-out same-distribution settings in the claim.
rows.check: The double-descent-shaped variance curve varies perturbation radius, not width, and does not measure V2's test-error behavior.

rows.subject: L-infinity adversarially trained models
rows.operation_detail: Evaluates bias, variance, and risk on CIFAR10-v6.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of ε.
rows.baseline: Standard CIFAR10 test dataset; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Bias and variance are similar to the standard test dataset case; variance decreases after ε = 10.
rows.note: The text does not provide numeric curve values.
rows.check: Distribution-shift effects on bias and variance do not measure a listed version. The reported ε = 10 corresponds to a radius of 10/255.

rows.subject: AugMix training models
rows.operation_detail: Varies AugMix augmentation severity and measures bias, variance, and risk on CIFAR10-C.
rows.measure: Bias, variance, and risk as functions of augmentation severity.
rows.baseline: Severity 0 corresponds to standard training; exact values not stated in text.
rows.value: Bias, variance, and risk monotonically decrease with increased augmentation severity.
rows.note: The paper contrasts this behavior with L-infinity adversarial training.
rows.check: AugMix severity effects do not test dropout addition or joint dropout/weight-decay removal in V6.
